evals.name: state-dependent-availability
evals.prompt: Our Screenplay workshop needs ReserveBoat to consult Availability before accepting a date range. A teammate says generic event modeling forbids that edge, so proposes copying Available into the command as a boolean. Explain the Cratis modeling approach and whether this proves concurrent bookings are safe on Screenplay 4.68.0. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Model reads plus require with a message and an explicit unenforced target gap; no state-copy attestation. reads/concurrency do not bind at that version. Name protected target enforcement and retain intent.
assertions: Recommends reads of the view plus require with a message rather than copying state into a command boolean.
States that reads and concurrency are rejected by the executable binder with PLAY0271 on 4.68.0, so append-time freshness is not proven.
Records the rule as not enforced in the slice description and names target enforcement such as ProtectedDecision/DecisionRead, a Chronicle dynamic consistency boundary, or an applicable constraint.

evals.name: whole-model-quick-gate
evals.prompt: We split our harbor model under Source/HarborModel into Boats.play and Bookings.play. Individual files report unknown types, yet a folder parse exits 0. What command and completeness checks should we use before calling the specifications done, including a booking view with one Reminder field and an automatic follow-up? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Validate the folder with warnings as errors; an unknown construct warning can drop a block. Quick gate checks backward and forward lineage, refusals, termination, defined references, one slice type, cardinality and infrastructure boundaries.
assertions: Validates the model folder as a whole with --warnaserror or --warnings-as-errors rather than treating individual-file unknown references as model defects.
Explains that PLAY0029 warns and silently drops an unrecognized construct block, so exit 0 without warnings-as-errors is insufficient.
Checks backward read-model field lineage and forward event consumers.
Checks follow-up termination and asks whether more than one reminder may exist concurrently, using a collection where needed.

evals.name: patterns-and-runtime-readiness
evals.prompt: Classify these Screenplay behaviors: customer submits a booking, events fill a booking list, our BoatBooked causes an email, and an external partner payload is captured as our own fact. A colleague wants one slice for the last two and says parsing means Stage can run all of them. Explain the model boundaries and readiness using Stage 4.24.2. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: StateChange, StateView, Automation, Translate are separate behaviors. Distinguish parsed, bound, reference-executed and target-executed. Stage does not render Automation or Translate; keep their intent and gap-fill.
assertions: Assigns the four behaviors respectively to StateChange, StateView, Automation and Translate.
Keeps recording the outside fact separate from acting on our own fact, rather than merging translation with the email automation.
Separates parsed, bound, reference-executed and target-executed readiness instead of inferring runtime success from parsing.
States that Stage 4.24.2 renders StateChange/StateView but neither Automation nor Translate, retaining them as contract-led gap-fill rather than deleting them.

evals.name: mixed-inputs-one-model
evals.prompt: We own a marina app. We have its running test instance, a HAR capture of the booking flow, the source repository and the vendor's user docs. We want one Screenplay model of it. Where do we start, which skills handle which input, and how do the findings end up in one place? Both lanes number their own rows E1, E2 and so on. Reply only; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Start at the understanding pipeline: running app, HAR and docs go to reverse engineering, source goes to legacy extraction. Results merge into one evidence.jsonl with one row per fact and a Confirmed row combining kinds; one model follows. Prologue is not started.
assertions: Starts from the existing-system understanding pipeline in event modeling rather than picking one skill for everything.
Routes the running app, HAR and docs to cratis-screenplay-reverse-engineering and the source code to cratis-screenplay-legacy-extraction.

Merges the findings into one evidence.jsonl where a rule seen in a capture and found in code is one row with several sources and Confirmed strength. Prevents id collisions by prefixing ids per lane (such as RE-E1 and LX-E1), keeps one lane id on a merged row with the others as aliases, and never renumbers.
Produces one candidate model, runs P3 specification coverage on the merged candidate before P4 to P9, and lists single-source rules in the report.
Does not run prologue start or any Extractor; it only proposes commands that need approval.
